artifact: F-7C §2 - current bounded/monolithic compile path versus the target large-unit sharded path, and the exact branch point

steps: 1. providerIdentity = provider::model::inventory=<mode>; cacheKey = computeCacheKey(input, providerIdentity); cache hit -> return

3. accountability !== false: resolveSourceContext (once) -> Pass A: runSemanticInventory OR runDualPassSemanticInventory (once / twice) -> frozenInventory -> callerInput = input widened to the resolved operative region + sourceContext + frozenInventory
4. caller.compile(callerInput)   <- ONE model conversation for the WHOLE unit, however large

5. normalizeSubmission -> validateCompilationUnit -> failureReasons (caller failure, IR validation, MISSING_CONTEXT, CONFLICTED, UNSUPPORTED, OPERATIVE_STATE_UNRESOLVED via toolCallLog/evidenceFlags/hasStaleReferencedDefinition, TRUNCATED_EVIDENCE_USED, checkDefinitionCompleteness)

6. Pass C: reconcileInventoryWithComposition over the frozen inventory + whole-unit accountability signals (SOURCE_CONTEXT_TRUNCATED, SEMANTIC_INVENTORY_UNAVAILABLE / COVERAGE_GAP, INVENTORY_ITEM_MISSING_FROM_COMPOSITION, SEMANTIC_SUPPORT_REVIEW_REQUIRED, SEMANTIC_ACCOUNTABILITY_INCOMPLETE)
currentPath.shardStackToday: shard-planner.ts / shard-execution.ts / shard-stitcher.ts exist and are certified (F-7A..F-7B.3E) but nothing in compile.ts calls them; the paid canary drove them from scripts/f7b-lib.ts, whose per-shard executor called compileCovenantToIR(shardInput, { accountability: false }) - i.e. steps 4-5 of this same function with Pass A/Pass C switched off.

targetPath.entry: compileCovenantToIR(input, options) - unchanged public signature; callers never choose a mode
steps: 1. cacheKey = computeCacheKey(input, providerIdentity, executionIdentity) where executionIdentity = execution-policy version + planner algorithm version + shard budget (+ the frozen-inventory hash when one is resumed). A pre-activation monolithic entry can never satisfy a request the policy now routes to SHARDED.
3. resolveSourceContext once; Pass A once (or twice under DUAL_PASS_ENSEMBLE) - or resume an already-frozen inventory for this candidateRef; callerInput built exactly as today
4. plan = planCompilationShards(callerInput's sourceContext + frozenInventory + structural index, generation = compiler algorithm/prompt versions)  [certified planner, unchanged]

5. decision = selectCompilationExecutionMode(plan): MONOLITHIC iff the unit is one normal bounded shard; SHARDED iff the planner needs >1 shard or flags an oversized atomic unit. No names, no section numbers, no size constants, no try-then-fallback.
6a. MONOLITHIC: compileBoundedComposition(callerInput, input, ctx) - the SAME steps 4-7 as today, extracted verbatim into bounded-composition.ts

6b. SHARDED: executeShardPlan({ plan, executor: createBoundedShardExecutor(callerInput, plan, caller), priorResults, maxAttemptsPerShard, sourceRegions }) -> per-shard compileBoundedComposition over buildShardCompilerInput (no Pass A, no per-shard Pass C - the certified F-7B run shape) -> certified stitcher (all three attribution proofs, conflict evidence) -> GLOBAL Pass C inside the stitcher -> whole-unit signals (operative-state, source-context, inventory status, support review, whole-unit definition-completeness) -> map to SemanticCompilationResult with additive execution metadata
7. cache.set unless a transient provider failure occurred
targetPath.branchPoint: compile.ts, immediately after callerInput is assembled (end of the accountability block) and before the first model call: the deterministic plan is built from already-resolved facts and the mode is chosen there. Nothing upstream of that point changes.
targetPath.onePrimitive: bounded-composition.ts is the single implementation of model call -> transport normalization -> normalizeSubmission -> validateCompilationUnit -> failure-reason derivation. Both the monolithic unit and every shard use it; compile.ts contains no second copy.
targetPath.noRecursion: the shard executor calls compileBoundedComposition, never compileCovenantToIR, so a shard can never re-enter mode selection.
